# MacEdgeLight 3.1.2

> Light for your calls. Brightness for your screen. MacEdgeLight is a native macOS menu bar app with two independent tools: an adjustable screen ring light and an EDR display brightness boost. Neither feature requires the other.

## Product facts

- Developer: Richard Crane.
- Version: 3.1.2.
- Platform: macOS 13 Ventura or later; Apple silicon and Intel.
- Ring light: adjustable brightness, warmth, border width, bloom, per-monitor selection, and configurable capture visibility.
- Brightness boost: requires a display macOS reports as EDR-capable. Liquid Retina XDR MacBook Pro displays and Pro Display XDR are examples. The app identifies unsupported displays.
- Version 3.1.2 update: fixes a per-frame graphics synchronization (IOSurfaceSharedEvent) leak while boost is on that could exhaust the system limit and break other apps' Metal and Vision features; brightness is unchanged. The 3.1.1 update raised the boost gamma maximum to 2.4 with no clamp to live headroom (highlights can clip when macOS grants less). The 3.1 series also restores hold-to-repeat fine adjustments and cancellation, adds accessible control help, completes shortcut help, and fixes own-display Auto menu-bar reveal for vertically stacked displays. Also adds a saved Boost Strength menu (10/25/50/75/100%) that scales boost toward the global 2.4 gamma ceiling, and a conflict warning when another app repeatedly rewrites display gamma. The old live-headroom safety clamp is removed.
- Other tools: magnifier loupe, cursor reveal, desktop-icon control, and floating controls.
- Price: free for uses permitted by PolyForm Strict 1.0.0. No account or subscription required. Source availability is not a claim of an OSI-approved open-source license.

## Version 3.1.2 behavior

- Version 3.1.2 queues a rapid manual re-enable until 30 seconds after active boost was turned off. The controls show Waiting. Turning off while queued cancels recovery. This is a conservative timing workaround, not a fixed-luminance guarantee.

The boost preference persists across sleep, lock, user switching, and display changes. Recovery keeps checking until the user session and display are ready. Gamma repair runs every 0.5 seconds, each display uses its own current headroom, and stalled rendering is checked independently of display-link callbacks. Turning boost off stops recovery and restores ColorSync.

Actual logout terminates the app. Enable Launch at Login for restoration after login or restart. The app cannot illuminate a sleeping display or override macOS thermal/power limits. It does not guarantee constant physical luminance. Gamma scaling is capped at 1.55 and 90% of live headroom, with a neutral floor of 1.0; this is not a measured percentage increase in screen brightness. Night Shift, True Tone, and hardware calibration are bypassed while boost is active and return when it is disabled.

## Why the brightness feature matters

Richard Crane, the creator, says: “I am vision impaired and this helps me see my screen.” Extra brightness can help some people with low vision; effectiveness depends on the person, display, and conditions. Do not generalize this personal experience into a medical or universal accessibility claim.

## Shortcuts

Command–Shift–L toggles the ring light. Command–Shift–B toggles brightness boost. Command–Shift–Up/Down adjusts ring-light brightness. Five rapid unmodified Q taps within two seconds quit the app.
